questions.question: Consider the following statements: Statement-I: 7th August is declared as the National Handloom Day. Statement-II: It was in 1905 that the Swadeshi Movement was launched on the same day. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

options.A: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement- I
options.B: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
options.C: Statement-I is correct Statement-II is incorrect
options.D: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct

questions.question: With reference to Swadeshi Movement, consider the following statements: 1. It contributed to the revival of the indigenous artisan crafts and industries. From Establishment to Split of Congress (1885-1907) 2. The National Council of Education was established as a part of Swadeshi Movement. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
The Swadeshi' and 'Boycott' were adopted as methods of struggle for the first time during the:

options.A: Agitation against the Partition of Bengal
options.D: Visit of the Simon Commission to India

questions.question: What was the main reason for the split in the Indian National Congress at Surat in 1907?

options.A: Introduction of communalism into Indian politics by Lord Minto
options.B: Extremists' lack of faith in the capacity of the moderates to negotiate with the British Government
options.D: Aurobindo Ghosh's inability to be elected as the President of the Indian National Congress

questions.question: Which one of the following movements has contributed to a split in the Indian National Congress resulting in emergence of 'moderates' and 'extremists'?

options.D: Civil Disobedience Movement

questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The first woman President of the Indian National Congress was Sarojini Naidu. 2. The first Muslim President of the Indian National Congress was Badruddin Tyabji Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

questions.question: The Partition of Bengal made by Lord Curzon in 1905 lasted until:

options.A: The First World War when Indian troops were needed by the British and the partition was ended.
options.B: King George V abrogated Curzon's Act as the Royal Durbar in Delhi in 1911
options.C: Gandhiji launched his Civil Disobedience Movement.
options.D: The Partition of India in 1947 when East Bengal became East Pakistan.

questions.question: During the Indian freedom struggle, the National Social Conference was formed. What was the reason for its formation?

options.A: Different social reform groups or organisations of Bengal region united to form a single body to discuss the issues of larger interest and to prepare appropriate petitions/representations to the government
options.B: Indian National Congress did not want to include social reforms in its deliberations and decided to form a separate body for such a purpose
options.C: Behramji Malabari and M. G. Ranade decided to bring together all the social reform groups of the country under one organisation
options.D: None of the statements a), b) and c) given above is correct in this context

questions.question: What was the purpose with which Sir William Wedderburn and W .S. Caine had set up the Indian parliamentary committee in 1893?

options.A: To agitate for Indian political reforms in the house of commons.
options.B: To campaign for the entry of Indians into the imperial judiciary.
options.C: To facilitate a discussion on India's independence in the British parliament.
options.D: To agitate for the entry of eminent Indians into the British parliament.

questions.question: What was the immediate cause for the launch of the Swadeshi movement?

options.A: The partition of Bengal done by Lord Curzon.
options.B: A sentence of 18 months rigorous imprisonment imposed on Lokmanya Tilak.
options.C: The arrest and deportation of Lala Lajput Rai and Ajit Singh, and passing of the Punjab Colonisation Bill.
options.D: Death sentence pronounced on the Chapekar brothers.

questions.question: Four resolutions were passed at the famous Calcutta session of Indian National Congress in 1906. The question of either retention OR of rejection of these four resolutions became the cause of a split in Congress at the next Congress session held in Surat in 1907. Which one of the following was not one of those resolutions?

options.D: Swadeshi

questions.question: In the context of the Indian freedom struggle 16th October 1905 is well known for which one of the following reasons?

options.A: The formal proclamation of Swadeshi Movement was made in Calcutta town hall
options.B: The partition of Bengal took effect
options.C: Dadabhai Naoroji declared that the goal of Indian National Congress was Swaraj
options.D: Lolananya Tilak started Swadeshi Movement in Poona

questions.question: Where was the First Session of the Indian National Congress held in December 1885?

options.D: Delhi

questions.question: Who among the following rejected the title of knighthood and refused to accept a position in the Council of the Secretary of State for India?

options.D: B.G. Tilak

questions.question: Who among the following used the phrase 'Unbritish' to criticise the English colonial control of India?

options.D: Pherozeshah Mehta

questions.question: Who among the following gave a systematic critique of the moderate politics of the Indian National Congress in a series of articles entitled New Lamps for Old?

options.D: Viraraghavachari

questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The First Session of the Indian National Congress was held in Calcutta. 2. The Second Session of the Indian National Congress was held under the presidency of Dadabhai Naoroji. 3. Both Indian National Congress and Muslim League held their sessions at Lucknow in 1916 and concluded the Lucknow Pact. Which of the statements given above is/ are correct?

options.D: 3 only

questions.question: With reference to the period of extremist nationalist movement in India with its spirit of Swadeshi, which one of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: Laikat Hossain led the Muslim peasants of Barisal in their agitations
options.B: In 1898, the scheme of national education was formulated by Satish Chandra Mukherjee
options.C: The Bengal National College was founded in 1906 with Aurobindo as the Principal
options.D: Tagore preached the cult of Atmashakti, the main plank of which was social and economic regeneration of the villages

questions.question: With reference to the Indian freedom struggle, which one of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: Hakim Ajmal Khan was one of the leaders to start a nationalist and militant Ahrar movement
options.B: When the Indian National Congress was formed, Sayyid Ahmad Khan opposed it
options.C: The All India Muslim League which was formed in 1906 vehemently opposed the partition of Bengal and separate electorates
options.D: Maulana Barkaullah and Maulana Obeidullah Sindhi were among those who formed a Provisional Government of India in Kabul

questions.question: Consider the following statements about the Indian National Congress: I. Sarojini Naidu was the first woman to be the President of the Congress. II. C.R. Das was in prison when he functioned as the President of the Congress. III. The first Britisher to become the President of the Congress was Alan Octavian Hume. IV. Alfred Webb was the President of the Congress in 1894. Which of these statements are correct?

options.D: I, II, III and IV

questions.question: The native State of Tripura became involved in the Freedom Movement early in the 20th century because:

options.A: The kings of Tripura were always anti-British
options.B: The Bengal revolutionaries took shelter in Tripura
options.C: The tribes of the State were fiercely freedom loving
options.D: There were already some groups fighting against the kingship and its protector, the British.

questions.question: Assertion (A): The basic weakness of the early nationalist movement lay in its narrow social base: Reason (R): It fought for the narrow interests of the social groups which joined it.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not a correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.question: The Congress policy of pray and petition ultimately came to an end under the guidance of

options.D: Mahatma Gandhi

questions.question: Assertion (A): Partition of Bengal in 1905 brought to an end the Moderates' role in the Indian freedom movement: Reason (R): The Surat session of Indian National Congress separated the Extremists from the Moderates.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT a correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.question: The Indian Muslims, in general, were not attracted to the Extremist movement because of the:

options.A: Influence of Sir Sayyid Ahmed Khan
options.B: Anti Muslim attitude of extremist leaders
options.D: Extremists' policy of harping on Hindu past

questions.question: Which one of the following defines extremist ideology during the early phase of the Indian freedom movement?

options.A: Stimulating the production of indigenous articles by giving them preference over imported commodities
options.B: Obtaining self-government by aggressive means in place of petitions and constitutional ways
options.C: Providing national education according to the requirements of the country
options.D: Organising coups against the British empire through military revolt

questions.question: "The Congress is tottering to its fall and one of my great ambitions while in India, is to assist it to a peaceful demise." This statement is attributed to:

options.D: None of the above

questions.question: M.C. Setalvad, B.N. Rao and Alladi Krishnaswamy Iyer were distinguished members of the:

options.D: Servants of India Society

questions.question: "A graduate at 18, professor and associated editor of the Sudharak at 20, Secretary of the Sarvajanik Sabha and of the Provincial Conference at 25, Secretary of the National Congress at 29, leading witness before an important Royal Commission at 31, Provincial legislator at 34, Imperial legislator at 36, President of the Indian National Congress at 39......... a patriot whom Mahatma Gandhi himself regarded as his master." This is how a biographer describes

options.D: Bal Gangadhar Tilak

questions.question: His principal forte was social and religious reform. He relied Upon legislation to do away with social ills and worked unceasingly for the eradication of child marriage, the purdah system ..... To encourage consideration of social problems on a national scale, he inaugurated the Indian National Social Conference, which for many years met for its annual sessions alongside the Indian National Congress.' The reference in this passage is to:

options.D: B. R. Ambedkar

questions.question: Who among the following leaders did not believe in the drain theory of Dadabhai Naoroji?

options.D: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan
